title: Short Stuff: Dolphin Detectors
summary: Short Stuff episode on how the U.S. Navy and other navies use dolphins to find (not disarm) underwater sea mines. The hosts explain dolphins locate mines with echolocation, signal the human handlers, and get a fish reward; a transponder is then attached to mark the mine. They trace the Navy's use of dolphins to a 1960 study on torpedo design, describe the dolphin-sea lion teams that also hunt underwater saboteurs, and discuss the harms of transporting dolphins, the moral objections, and an animal rights protest in Puget Sound involving knitted sweaters.

segments.title: Opening banter and dolphin mine-finding setup
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter, then introduce the topic: the U.S. Navy and other militaries use dolphins to find underwater mines, not to disarm them.

segments.title: How dolphins find and mark mines
segments.summary: Dolphins are trained to locate mines, signal handlers with a bell or flare, and then guide a transponder placed on the mine. They receive a fish as a reward.

segments.title: Dolphin echolocation compared to human sonar
segments.summary: The hosts explain that dolphins use echolocation, producing clicks through the nasal passages and focusing them through the melon, then receiving echoes through a fat passage in the jaw to the inner ear. They say dolphins can distinguish a BB pellet from a corn kernel at about fifty feet.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: A short break before the second half of the episode.

segments.title: Navy origins of dolphin program and transport concerns
segments.summary: The Navy began using dolphins after a 1960 study on whether dolphin movement could improve torpedo design; the study found nothing for torpedoes but led to training dolphins for mine detection. The hosts then discuss the stress of transporting dolphins between oceans and the animal welfare concerns.

segments.title: Dolphin-sea lion teams, saboteurs, and Puget Sound protest
segments.summary: The hosts describe naval teams pairing dolphins and sea lions to catch underwater saboteurs, and a planned Puget Sound patrol in Washington State that drew an animal rights protest, including knitted sweaters for the dolphins.

segments.title: Closing remarks and listener contact
segments.summary: The hosts summarize that dolphins find rather than disarm mines, note the moral debate, and invite listeners to email the show.
